summary: Uses PLEXOS; the source does not say for what.
why_it_supports_the_claim: Prayas (Energy Group), a Pune-based Indian non-profit policy research organization (registered SIRO under India's Dept of Scientific and Industrial Research), directly built and ran its own PLEXOS model of the Maharashtra power system in 2019, prior to migrating to the open-source GridPath platform for a 2021 follow-up study. The 2021 report's own methodology section states: 'The model is set up in a way similar to that in an earlier study by the authors using the commercial power system modelling platform, PLEXOS (PEG, 2019) (Dukkipati, Dixit, Gambhir, & Chitnis, 2019)...The earlier PLEXOS model is modified with the same inputs as the GridPath model, and the results from both these models are compared. The versions of these platforms used for this analysis are version 0.8.2 of GridPath and version 7.500R04 of PLEXOS' [10]. Independently corroborated by Prayas's own December 2019 webinar description (same Dukkipati/Gambhir/Dixit authorship): 'This exercise involved granular (15 min block) system simulation using the PLEXOS platform and shows that 50% of electricity demand can be met by RE sources without any adverse economic or reliability implications' [11]. Historical: the original PLEXOS study dates to 2019; Prayas's own 2021 report explicitly states they subsequently moved to the open-source GridPath platform citing commercial-tool cost and black-box transparency concerns for Indian stakeholders ('Commercial tools, though popular and feature-rich, are unaffordable to a wide range of stakeholders in India...the black box nature of these closed-source tools makes them unsuitable for public consultation processes'), so no evidence of continuing PLEXOS use was found -- flagged historical rather than current. Second-pass applied given the historical/discontinued-use nuance: role classified as research_user (non-profit policy research institute performing its own first-party PLEXOS modelling for a published study), parallel to the Makerere University precedent, not reclassified to direct_user despite Prayas not being a university, since 'direct_user' in the existing taxonomy is more commonly reserved for operational/commercial/governmental entities; this distinction is noted for curator review.

why_it_supports_the_claim: MENA/Gulf new hit found via a systematic IRENA/CIF/GCF/USAID/GIZ sweep (searching IRENA Gulf-states renewable-integration studies led to this primary source). EWEC (the single buyer and seller of water and electricity in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi) states in its own official 2021-2027 Statement of Future Capacity Requirements: 'In preparing this Statement, all modelling work has been carried out by the EWEC planning team with drafting support from NERA Economic Consulting.' The document explicitly names 'The PLEXOS power and water system production cost model, to evaluate optimal capacity expansion projects' as one of two analytical models used, and repeatedly describes PLEXOS results in first person ('Our PLEXOS modelling suggests...', 'Since the 2019 Statement, we have made a number of improvements to the PLEXOS modelling infrastructure'). NERA Economic Consulting provided only drafting support (not modeling) per EWEC's own acknowledgment, so NERA is not recorded as consultant_modeler for this engagement -- EWEC's own planning team is the party that built and ran the PLEXOS model, warranting direct_user. This upgrades MENA/UAE coverage beyond the prior academic-only evidence (Heriot-Watt Dubai research_user, ORG-AFME-0016): EWEC is a genuine government-adjacent utility (single buyer/seller for Abu Dhabi, reporting to the Department of Energy) running its own PLEXOS model for official annual capacity planning, not a third-party research study. Current: 2021-2027 Statement is the latest in an annual series dating to at least 2019, with PLEXOS modelling explicitly continuing ('we have made a number of improvements to the PLEXOS modelling infrastructure' since 2019).

summary: Commissioned a PLEXOS study to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study.
source_title: Hawai’I Asia pacific Regional Energy System Assessment (APRESA)  ASEAN Interconnection Masterplan Study (AIMS) III Support
exact_snippet_or_quote: HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE), an intergovernmental organization within the ASEAN structure representing the AMS interests in the energy sector, on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study.
why_it_supports_the_claim: DEDICATED FOLLOW-UP per unresolved_questions.md batch63_regional_subject flag: investigated ACE itself (Jakarta-based ASEAN intergovernmental secretariat), not the ASEAN member states, as a direct_user/commissioner candidate for the AIMS III regional PLEXOS study. ACE's own AIMS III Phase 1&2 Report states 'The Head of the ASEAN Power Utilities/Authorities (HAPUA) Council appointed the ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) as the Implementing Agency (IA)' and 'The AIMS III Report was jointly developed by ACE and the national experts from the ASEAN Member States as part of the AIMS III Working Group, with GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant' [2]. 'The capacity expansion planning task was made with PLEXOS using Energy Exemplar as the simulation tool' [2] -- confirming PLEXOS as the actual tool used to build the AIMS III capacity-expansion model. ACE's own news page independently corroborates that ACE selected and directed GE Energy Consulting as the PLEXOS-running consultant: 'ACE with its selected consultant to lead the works of AIMS III, GE Consortium, wisely welcomed the inputs and feedbacks from all TRG members' [3]. HNEI/GridSTART's own project page confirms ACE itself received hands-on PLEXOS training, but frames it as management-oversight capacity rather than production modeling: 'HNEI GridSTART provided training to the ASEAN Center for Energy (ACE)...on production cost analysis and use of the PLEXOS software tool to empower ACE personnel to more effectively carry out project management duties for the AIMS III study' [1]. ROLE JUDGMENT (8-question evaluator checklist applied): (1) Is PLEXOS named? Yes, explicitly and repeatedly in ACE's own report. (2) Is the org named as doing something specific with it? Yes -- ACE is named as the appointing/directing Implementing Agency that selected and managed the PLEXOS-running consultant (GE Energy Consulting), and procured PLEXOS-proficiency from that consultant via its own RFP (per unresolved_questions.md's prior citation of ACE's 2018 RfP language). (3) Did ACE itself build/operate the production PLEXOS model? No -- the report attributes the actual capacity-expansion PLEXOS simulation work to 'GE Energy Consulting and Consortium as the consultant', not to ACE directly; the PLEXOS training ACE personnel received is explicitly scoped to 'project management duties' (i.e. overseeing/reviewing the consultant's work), not independently running production AIMS III simulations. Unlike a generic consultancy job posting listing PLEXOS alongside competing tools as candidate background (the catalogue's standard false-positive risk, per the plexos-org-catalogue-research skill), this is a GOVERNMENT AGENCY's own stated job duties for operating PLEXOS as part of its own national IRRP -- the agency itself, not a hired consultant, is the entity described as running the software. exact_snippet_or_quote: The paper addresses resilience assessment of a power system due to disruption of interconnecting power lines.The power system analysed is based on an anonymized EU region well interconnected with other Member States.We analyse several disruption scenarios and rank them by introducing a resilience index.The selected disruptions are modelled using the -open source -PyPSA-Eur software tool.The study aims to quantify and rank importance of interconnecting supply routes to the security of power supply in the analysed region.
